notes: DISPLAY FIX: the Emergency cover breakdown showed a negative liquid-investment balance. SYMPTOM: liquid money Rs 6,33,383 was itemised as cash and savings Rs 12,13,119 plus investments marked liquid MINUS Rs 5,79,736. A negative investment balance is impossible, and the cash line exceeded the total it belonged to. CAUSE: the two sub-lines were computed as cashOnly = raw engine cashSeries, and liquidInv = liquid - cashSeries. That derivation was valid while the liquid series was BUILT from cashSeries, because subtracting it back out left exactly the liquid investments. When v2026.05.08.02 repointed _dcLiquidSeries at the shared savings chain, this subtraction was not updated, so it began differencing two unrelated series. The negative figure was therefore not a balance at all — it was precisely the Rs 5,79,736 gap between the raw engine series and the real chain, the very discrepancy that version fixed, resurfacing in the display. SCOPE: the total and the verdict were always correct. Liquid investments are still added to the series, so the Rs 6,33,383 figure and the Rs 2,36,138 shortfall stood; only the itemisation beneath them was wrong. On a portfolio with every instrument marked illiquid the total is unaffected either way, which is why this surfaced as a cosmetic oddity rather than a wrong decision. FIX: the split is now taken from the two components directly rather than derived by subtraction. A dedicated _dcLiquidInvSeries returns the liquid-investment component, and cash is the remainder of the series after removing it. Verified both ways: with every instrument illiquid the breakdown reads cash Rs 9,20,764 and investments Rs 0; with mutual funds marked liquid it reads the same cash plus Rs 7,63,499 of investments. The cash figure is identical across both, the parts sum to the total, and the investment figure is never negative. GENERAL LESSON, worth recording: deriving one displayed quantity by subtracting another is fragile. It held only while both came from the same source, and failed silently the moment one was repointed. Where two numbers are shown as the parts of a whole, both should be computed from their own source. Regression confirms the Projection-to-Dashboard gap and the Decisions-to-chain gap both remain zero. Engine, runProjection and the four decision tests are untouched. No page errors.
